Wonderzoekers is a playful, kid-friendly podcast series in which Sofie Palmers & Katrien Pierlet marvel at the inner workings of the human mind. In addition to the podcast, they’re also turning it into a theater production. In this live episode, they—along with their guests—take you on a journey into the fascinating world of The Lie . An adventurous, scientific, and occasionally out-there quest to uncover the truth behind the lie.

Lying… we all do it sometimes. Sometimes to spare someone’s feelings, sometimes to get ourselves out of trouble. But did you know there are tricks for exposing a lie? Sofie and Katrien give you handy tips on how to lie better and explore whether a well-told lie can be just as powerful as the truth.

In addition to the story of The Lie , you’ll also get a behind-the-scenes look. In this show, you’ll actually see them recording a podcast live: with microphones, live music, and artisanal foley sounds. After all, what does a professional liar sound like? And what does sneaking a taste of candy at the supermarket or telling a white lie sound like? Katrien and Sofie pull out all the stops—literally—to create that one perfect sound. And sometimes, you can just close your eyes and listen.

Sofie Palmers (SKaGeN, fABULEUS, …) and Katrien Pierlet (Studio Orka, Ultima Thule, …) have both made their mark in the theater world. Their love of storytelling took them from the stage to the world of audio.
1D6EBFD0AF94D19FBA2660C8910BBB4C:
Everyone has their own rhythm. But what happens when those rhythms intersect? A flamenco dancer and a stepper let their bodies speak as percussion instruments: they build up an exhilarating dance full of complex pulsating rhythms.

Live electronic sounds drive them forward – sometimes supporting them, sometimes challenging them, always surprising them.

Re:Beat doesn’t stop at the edge of the stage. Everyone is invited to join in. To feel how rhythm flows through the body. To discover how it moves, collides and connects.

After FeL and FRAMED , choreographer Karolien Verlinden returns to hetpaleis with a new rhythmic project. Re:Beat is a body score as a shared sensory experience. In the playful encounter between rhythms and dance styles, a story emerges about singularity and difference, collaboration and empathy – tailored to everyone with a heartbeat.
226264F4E61DFBDD7BD5C986AD6AE51A:
Every year, countless spruces and pine trees are felled, but what do those trees themselves actually think about this? Do they queue up every year, eagerly waiting to be chosen, or do they cower behind one another, only to be felled anyway?

In Oh oh oh dennenboom , we get to know the trees in the forest. There is the elder tree – once uprooted and replanted – who is now the source of all information about what goes on among humans (played by Hendrik Kegels). There is a suicidal tree, which is just dying to be chopped down, but which, with three scrawny branches, is unsuitable for Christmas (played by Frank Focketyn).

And then the felling season begins; the tragedy has started. But this year is different. This year, they’ve had enough! Time for a pine revolution. Will the trees succeed in establishing new traditions among humans?
3F4250034606081915D7A4472098693B:
A change was coming, and nobody knew it but me.

Constance Doenkerbos loves her sister Meerkat and her cousin Sjarel. Uncle Jul loves writing very much, but he doesn’t love Sjarel. And Meerkat doesn’t like her cousin at all. Oh no, she loves dangerous mushrooms, mad kings and magic spells. The Doenkerbos family lives a secluded life on an estate on the outskirts of the village. There used to be seven of them, but four family members were mysteriously poisoned.

Since then, the villagers have treated the Doenkerbos family with suspicion and hostility; only Meerkat still dares to leave the estate. When Sjarel starts acting strangely, sparks really start to fly …

Stef Lernous previously created Bangerik and Groezel for hetpaleis. Now he has adapted the last book of Shirley Jackson, the American author of blood-curdling stories. With CASTL , the novel is being staged for the first time by a first-rate cast: Janne Desmet, Lotte Diependaele, Bart Hollanders, Manou Kersting and Maja Westerveld.

Every first Sunday of the month, we make sure hetpaleis is extra cosy.

Six well-known and lesser-known artists read aloud from their favourite children’s book. This is followed by a (craft) workshop based on the story that’s just been read.

PS: coming and going is no problem, and you don’t have to sit still either.
